set.st: Two hermit brothers, trappers and well-diggers, lived on a 10-acre farm 3 mi SW of Palmyra. After the last died in Nov 1926, more than $5,000 was found: old gold notes between attic timbers, gold in soldered gas-pipe cylinders under a floorboard, and more in old shoes and tin cans. Searchers suspected more, and the yard was to be dug in the spring of 1927; no report of that dig. Pin is the likely lot, fitted from the neighbours, not the spot itself. AP, 19 Feb 1927: more than $5,000 had been found. It included gold notes of 1863 and soldered pipes of gold coin under a floor board ($588 in one find). Villagers tore up the floors, walls and the swamp around the shack, and the sheriff posted guards. The surviving brother went to England.
set.pl: Small unlabelled lot by the sec 30/31 line, W-central Palmyra Twp, between P. Peterson (sec 30) and C. Thayer (sec 31) on the c.1915 Hixson plat, fitted from the 1920 census order; 3 mi SW of Palmyra
pinev: c.1915 Hixson plat, Palmyra Twp T5N R16E: 'P. Peterson 40' S-central sec 30 (and P. Peterson 33 at the W edge); 'Cliff Thayer 87' N part of sec 31 just S of Peterson; small unlabelled lots sit by the road on the sec 30/31 line.

1920 census, Palmyra Twp: Albert Blackmore (b. 1846 England, single, owns free) and brother Charley (b. 1856), enumerated in the order Pettersen, Blackmore, Thayer, which puts the brothers' 10 acres on or near the sec 30/31 line, W-central; lot unlabelled, so inferred from neighbours.
